label: Illustrative planning multipliers - NOT calibrated coefficients and NOT scientific forecasts
provenance: TerraLex backend/app/config/scenario_multipliers.json (configurable, bounds-validated). No observational calibration, no peer-reviewed source, no site measurements.
usage_note: Every value below is an assumption chosen for scenario comparison only. Change it and the label 'modelled' still applies. Multipliers are applied to mapped/user-provided geography and never presented as measurements.

land_take_factor.label: Land take factor
land_take_factor.basis: Planning assumption: how much more/less land the scenario occupies relative to the user footprint.

water_intensity_factor.label: Water intensity factor
water_intensity_factor.basis: Planning assumption scaling the user-declared water demand (MLD). Derived here as preset MLD / baseline MLD.

energy_intensity_factor.label: Energy intensity factor
energy_intensity_factor.basis: Planning assumption scaling the user-declared power demand (MW). Derived here as preset MW / baseline MW.

site_disturbance_factor.label: Construction disturbance fraction
site_disturbance_factor.basis: Planning assumption: share of the site area cleared/graded during construction. Not a survey or an EIA figure.

vegetation_retention_factor.label: Vegetation retention fraction
vegetation_retention_factor.basis: Planning assumption: share of mapped tree cover inside the footprint that is retained. Applied to ESA WorldCover tree-cover area when available.

impervious_surface_factor.label: Impervious surface fraction
impervious_surface_factor.basis: Planning assumption: share of the site area sealed by buildings, hardstanding and roads. Not a drainage design figure.

baseline.label: Baseline
baseline.description: User-declared project, no growth and no mitigation.

high-growth.label: High growth
high-growth.description: Expanded campus with water-cooled plant - the most land-, water- and energy-intensive comparison case.

mitigation.label: Mitigation
mitigation.description: Same campus with hybrid-dry cooling, recycled water and retained vegetation.
